cases.answer: The meta-analysis (Sabaté-Ortega et al., Front Oncol 2025) was a systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 observational studies using real-world data, covering 23,621 NSCLC patients. Of these, 3 were prospective and 9 were retrospective. Searches ran to 21 November 2023, and a random-effects model was used. Among ICI-treated patients, the pooled prevalence of CV events was 3% (95% CI 3%-4%; p<0.00001; I2=96%). The pooled hazard ratio versus patients treated with other (non-ICI) drugs was 1.78 (95% CI 1.46-2.17; p<0.00001; I2=72%). Subtype estimates include the following. Prevalence: pericardial disease 3%, myocarditis 1%, arrhythmia 3%, heart failure 2%, VTE 9%. HR: peri-/myocarditis 5.51 (2.85-10.65), CV death 3.44 (2.15-5.5), heart failure 1.78 (1.17-2.68). The limitations section says only 4 studies were used for the HR analysis.

cases.answer: The Batra review cites a meta-analysis of 30 NSCLC studies (n=3,287; Lu et al., 2025). Sensitivity was similar for tumor-informed and tumor-agnostic assays at the landmark timepoint (42% vs 44%) and longitudinally (76% vs 79%). Tumor-informed assays had higher specificity at both timepoints: landmark 97% vs 93%, longitudinal 96% vs 88%.
